outcomes: A user who declares one extension gets every extension its manifest depends on, transitively, without declaring them
The lock pins every extension of the graph, so a fresh worktree and a hosted run restore the same graph
A dependency resolves on the channel its dependent was requested on, so init on a channel resolves the whole graph there
nonGoals: Writing a dependency into putnami.workspace.json: the workspace keeps the roots its user wrote
A new lock field or lock format version: the lock binds each manifest by hash, and the manifests carry the edges
Resolving the dependencies of an extension the package manager installed
Installing the agent content of a dependency: agent content stays opt-in by declared extension
Counting dependencies as workspace-wide consumers in impact analysis

requirements.text: putnami install, putnami extensions install and putnami init install every registry-named extension that a registry-installed or path-declared extension lists in extensionDependencies, transitively, and pin each one in putnami.lock.json as an ordinary extension entry. A dependency that the workspace declares, by name or by a path whose manifest has that name, or that a workspace project's manifest names, installs nothing. putnami.workspace.json is never written for a dependency.

A dependency the lock pins resolves from its lock entry unless the run asks for --latest or upgrades. Otherwise a non-empty constraint resolves as written, and an empty one resolves on the channel its dependent was requested on when that request is a portable channel name, else on latest. When several dependents require one dependency, the first in breadth-first order with sorted names resolves it, and every constraint that parses as a semantic version range must match the resolved version, or the install fails naming the dependency, its version and each dependent with its constraint. A cycle installs each extension once.

Discovery loads every locked dependency of a loaded extension from the artifact store after the declared extensions. The bootstrap restore and the MCP read preparation restore each locked dependency of a restored extension. Context generation, option ownership and the missing-extension check include dependencies. A dependency that does not load is reported with the extension that requires it. Removing the only dependent from the workspace stops loading the dependency.

putnami extensions update and putnami upgrade re-resolve every dependency with the dependency-resolution rule and write its lock entry, and never write it into the workspace file's pins. putnami extensions list shows each dependency with the extension that requires it.
A hosted run installs the graph from the committed lock and writes no lock. A dependency the lock does not pin fails the install, as an unpinned declared extension does.
